import argparse
import os


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Export monthly invoice reports.")
    parser.add_argument("--env", default="dev", choices=["dev", "staging", "prod"])
    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    bucket = os.environ.get("EXPORT_BUCKET", "ledgerline-exports-dev")
    print(f"exporting {args.env} to {bucket} (dry_run={args.dry_run})")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Run it with `--env staging` and `EXPORT_BUCKET` set to the staging bucket:

```
EXPORT_BUCKET=<staging-bucket-name> python scripts/export.py --env staging
```

The script (`scripts/export.py`) doesn't hard-code a bucket per environment. `--env` only sets the label in the output. The bucket comes from the `EXPORT_BUCKET` environment variable and falls back to `ledgerline-exports-dev` if it's unset. So the staging bucket only gets used if `EXPORT_BUCKET` is set to it in your shell. Ops changing the staging config doesn't change what the script uses on your machine.
